items.title: Google Updates AI Recipe Results To Send More Traffic
items.summary: Google has revamped AI Mode recipe results to feature a side panel with images, summaries, and tappable links to original recipe sites, addressing complaints about synthesized content dominating responses. This change promotes more traffic to creators by making site links more discoverable. Content marketers in the recipe niche should optimize structured data and visuals to leverage these AI referrals.

items.title: Google Search Ranking Volatility Continues Into March 2026: What the Data Shows and What to Do Now
items.summary: Tracking tools report persistent high volatility in Google search rankings extending into early March 2026, with SEMrush Sensor hitting 9.5 and significant traffic losses, tied to the recent Discover core update and speculation of a new core update. The update prioritizes local, expert-driven content over clickbait. SEOs are advised to audit for topical authority, enhance content depth, and track performance closely.

items.title: AI and SEO: What AI means for the future of SEO [Expert Tips & Interview]
items.summary: AI-driven search features like overviews are boosting zero-click rates to 69% and shifting traffic to LLMs, forecasted to eclipse Google by 2027, demanding AEO and GEO tactics such as structured content and intent-focused optimization. Marketers must prioritize machine-readable data, original insights, and multi-platform authority to remain visible. Tools like AI Search Grader help evaluate performance in generative engines.

items.title: The March 2026 “Discover” Update: Is Your SME AI-Proof?
items.summary: Google's March 2026 Discover update emphasizes topical consolidation across sites, a Home Turf Filter for local relevance, and penalties for thin AI-generated content, favoring original expertise with elements like local images. SMEs should implement high-resolution original visuals, entity schema linking to local entities, and non-clickbait headlines. This evolves AEO by assessing entire digital footprints for authority.

items.title: Generative Engine Optimization: The New Era of Search
items.summary: GEO optimizes content for citation in AI responses from tools like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews, capitalizing on their massive usage and influence on decisions, overlapping with SEO via quality content, accessibility, and backlinks. Tactics include quotes, stats, fresh content, and unlinked mentions, tracked via Semrush's AI Visibility tools. As AI search grows, GEO ensures brand presence beyond traditional rankings.

items.title: Two Rivers to Sell and Distribute Guinness World Records
items.summary: Ingram's Two Rivers Distribution has entered a sales and distribution agreement with Guinness World Records Limited for the U.S. market, effective May 1, 2026. The partnership follows strong sales of the 2026 edition, with 260,000 units shipped, and upcoming releases like a Soccer Edition and Gamer's Edition. Executives from both sides expressed optimism about expanding the brand's U.S. presence.

items.title: Sarah J. Maas announces two new 'A Court of Thorns and Roses' books
items.summary: Fantasy author Sarah J. Maas announced on the Call Her Daddy podcast that two new books in the A Court of Thorns and Roses (ACOTAR) series are forthcoming, with book six releasing on October 27, 2026, and book seven on January 12, 2027. She described the story as a single expansive narrative with ongoing arcs. BookTok fans are reacting intensely, with speculation flooding TikTok, Reddit, and X.

items.title: Reading is so trendy now that Coach is making book charms
items.summary: Coach has launched a Spring 2026 campaign featuring $95 miniature book-shaped bag charms with classics like Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility, partnering with Penguin Random House and other publishers. The charms capitalize on BookTok and Bookstagram trends where reading serves as an aesthetic and performative signal amid digital overload. Some titles sold out quickly, highlighting the intersection of luxury branding and book culture.

items.title: Book Release Radar: Most anticipated reads of March 2026
items.summary: March 2026 highlights include Yann Martel's Son of Nobody, a Trojan War retelling; Tana French's The Keeper, final in the Cal Hooper series and recommended on BookTok for thrillers; and Abby Jimenez's romance The Night We Met. These releases span epic fantasy, mystery, and contemporary romance, generating early buzz. The Night We Met is set for March 31.

items.title: Distribution Deals for the Week of Mar. 2, 2026
items.summary: Publishers Weekly reports key deals: Lakeside Book Company signed with Fulcrum Publishing, Mythworks, and Oak Tree Comics effective March 1; Jaguar Book Group to distribute Schiffer Publishing in Canada from April 1. These agreements alongside Two Rivers' Guinness deal signal active expansion in distribution networks. Hornblower Group will handle sales representation for Schiffer in Canada.

items.title: Disney Cancels Likely Woke Live-Action Robin Hood Remake
items.summary: Disney has canceled its live-action Robin Hood project, a musical reimagining in development since 2020 intended for Disney+. The decision comes amid financial flops and audience backlash to recent woke-leaning remakes like Snow White and The Little Mermaid. The studio is reassessing its strategy for such adaptations.

items.title: 'A Knight of Seven Kingdoms' Actress Responds to Racial Backlash Over Casting
items.summary: Tanzyn Crawford, playing Tanselle in HBO's Game of Thrones prequel, faced online backlash regarding her race for the Dornish character. The show has been celebrated by some for its non-woke focus on white male leads, contrasting with other fantasy series. George R.R. Martin endorsed her casting as matching his vision from the source material.

items.title: Scary Movie 6 Trailer Draws Backlash for Pronoun Joke
items.summary: The Scary Movie 6 trailer features a scene mocking pronouns during a Ghostface attack, sparking outrage from viewers calling it transphobic and outdated. Supporters defend it as classic franchise satire targeting woke culture. Original cast returns for the June release amid divided reactions.

items.title: Twenty One Pilots Concert Film Tops Elvis Presley Doc at Box Office
items.summary: Twenty One Pilots' film outperformed Baz Luhrmann's Elvis Presley documentary EPiC, grossing strong numbers despite reviews. The 2000s rock duo's draw highlights enduring fan interest in live music experiences. It marks a surprise win in recent box office trends.

items.title: Fans Critique Paramount's Woke Influence on Star Trek and CBS Shows
items.summary: Audiences highlight Paramount's push of woke elements in Star Trek series like Discovery and Starfleet Academy, alongside CBS reboots emphasizing female empowerment. Shows like Halo TV and Grease reboot faced criticism for identity politics. Discussion arises amid potential Warner Bros merger talks.

items.title: Disney Faces 'Go Woke, Go Broke' Sentiment Over Family Content
items.summary: Observers note Disney's shift to preachy content alienating families, leading to brand damage and calls for executive overhaul. Families opt for classic films over new releases amid luxury pricing for divisive stories. Generational pushback favors broad appeal reminiscent of earlier eras.

items.title: Small Business Technology News: Intuit Launches AI-Powered ERP Solution Tailored For Construction Industry
items.summary: Intuit has launched a new Construction Edition for its Intuit Enterprise Suite, an AI-native ERP solution designed to support mid-market construction companies by combining project, financial, and operational workflows in one system. It includes AI-powered processes and industry-specific tools such as cost proposals, invoicing, and budgeting. This offering provides a scalable path for construction businesses growing out of QuickBooks, integrating AI to streamline complex needs.

items.title: VistaPrint Launches New Generative AI Logomaker, Turning Small Business Ideas Into Professional, Print-Ready Logos in Minutes
items.summary: VistaPrint has launched AI Logomaker, a generative AI logo design tool created specifically for small businesses to bypass generic templates and complex prompts. It enables entrepreneurs to build personalized, high-quality logos using simple user prompts, with access to free digital and print-ready files. The tool provides an intuitive experience, creative control through editing capabilities, and integration with VistaPrint's print services.

items.title: How NYC Small Businesses Are Putting AI to Work for Them
items.summary: New York City small businesses and nonprofits are adopting AI through training programs like the Manhattan Chamber of Commerce's Tech to Table and Decoded Futures to enhance efficiency without job cuts, such as using AI for inventory management, sales tracking, and marketing. Examples include Holly Diamond's Korean restaurant in Flatiron, where AI improves menus, handles inquiries in multiple languages, and streamlines hiring via an HR app; Welcome to Chinatown, which uses AI tools like Claude to conduct neighborhood surveys, manage data zones, and automate event bookings. These initiatives, supported by grants and tech mentors, have enabled tools like Diamond's app to be used by over 15,000 businesses and job seekers.
